newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice futures end mixed, exports supportive.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice futures end mixed, exports supportive.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended a quiet session mixed with weakness tied to bear spreading and strength linked to USDA weekly export sales data that came in above expectations, traders said.
"Export sales were decent this morning and it was all long grain," a trader said.
USDA on Thursday put weekly export sales at 22,300 tonnes, below the previous week. But rough rice, the variety traded on the exchange, dominated the purchases.
Mexico, the Netherlands and Nicaragua were the primary buyers, USDA said.
Trade was said to be quiet as traders and end-users prepared for a trade convention in California.
"Everybody's clearing out to California," one source said.
The market continued to watch weather patterns in India where the monsoon season still had not begun. Without sufficient monsoon rains, India's rice crop could deteriorate, traders said.
Rice ended 2-1/2 cents per cwt lower to one cent higher with July off 2-1/2 at $11.57 per cwt. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 150 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 261.
